dedupe_keys.name: mosicas sugarcane crop growth model r cirad

description: MOSICAS is a simple crop model for annual or semi-perennial giant C4 crops such as sugarcane, written in R. The Zenodo record says it simulates biomass growth driven by the soil water balance and air temperature: plant parameters tell whether the crop is a first planting or a regrowth after harvest, daily leaf area index growth sets intercepted radiation, which is turned into dry mass with a radiation use efficiency, and carbon is split into roots, leaves, stem and sugar reserves. It needs daily temperature, precipitation, global radiation and evapotranspiration, with soil water holding capacity and soil depth; the full description is on CIRAD GitLab. Version 1.1.0 (14 April 2025) adds automatic irrigation calculation and is a downloadable ZIP of about 0.1 MB under CC BY 4.0, by Mathias Christina of CIRAD. Coverage is any sugarcane site with those inputs. Caveats: a simple model without nutrient limits named on the record read. For simulation it estimates sugarcane yield and irrigation needs under drought, and the cane supply that sugar mills and their power plants depend on. Related catalogue records include AquaCrop and DSSAT.
